[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 65[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to another Hack Forum News edition. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6331756][color=#ffffff]BTCPay for Members (Vendors please read)[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

BTCPay has been Hack Forums main invoicing system [mention=1] is now considering building a dedicated server for members, Vendors would receive free access while store subscriptions could also be made available for around $10 a month using the new monetization feature. This could also bring automated crypto invoicing straight to Hack Forums contracts still your keys and your wallets with no funds being held. Would you consider making use of this? Share your thoughts and feedback in the original thread.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6331761][color=#ffffff]CTF Challenge Winners[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

The drawings for the CanYouHack.Me challenges are officially complete awarding a total of $800 in crypto currency along with 6 permanent upgrades. Big congratulations to [mention=3382541] for taking home the top $250 prize as well as [mention=3539763] & [mention=4568478] & [mention=2195096] for winning $100 each. Additional $50 prizes and permanent L33t/Ub3r upgrades have also been distributed to qualifying participants. Thank you to everyone who participated and to CanYouHack.Me for hosting the challenges. Be sure to check the original thread to see the full list of winners.

Blizzard revealed a new iteration of WoW launching later this year on November 4.

[u][b][size=large]Marvel's Wolverine[/size][/b][/u]

Insomniac Games highly anticipated standalone superhero action title finally hits shelves, dominating the conversation for PlayStation 5 players.

[u][b][size=large]Subscription Cancellations Surge[/size][/b][/u]

A new market data report revealed that over 40% of users who cancelled their Xbox Game Pass, PlayStation Plus, or Nintendo Switch Online subscriptions this quarter blamed rising costs.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]AI companies are thinking of Slowing things down[/color][/size][/b][/u]

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for AI companies to slow the pace of advanced-AI development, citing safety concerns. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk have also expressed support for greater caution, although the companies don't necessarily agree on what regulation should look like. There's also growing disagreement internationally. Germany has said that simply stopping AI development isn't viable, while China has criticised calls for a slowdown as potentially serving US interests.

[b][url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/foldable-iphone-pricier-18-pro-unveiled-apples-first-event-under-ternus-2026-09-09]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Apple launches its first foldable iPhone[/color][/size][/b][/u]

Apple's biggest hardware event of the year happened last week, with the company unveiling its first foldable iPhone, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and other hardware. The event was also notable because it was the first major iPhone launch under new CEO John Ternus, giving investors a look at Apple's strategy as it tries to catch up in AI.

[b][url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/foldable-iphone-pricier-18-pro-unveiled-apples-first-event-under-ternus-2026-09-09]Source[/url][/b]
